fw-grandpa-001.front: Finish Grandpa's saying: "Treat every firearm as if it is ..."

fw-grandpa-002.back: Never point a gun at anything you do not want to shoot. Tradition: Control the muzzle (85%).

fw-grandpa-003.front: What must you know besides your target?
fw-grandpa-003.back: What is beyond it. Look past the animal; the sky is never a backstop. Tradition (85%).

fw-grandpa-004.front: Where does your trigger finger live until you decide to shoot?
fw-grandpa-004.back: Straight along the stock, outside the trigger guard. Tradition: the T in ACTS (85%).

fw-grandpa-014.front: Wind check shows a swirl. Grandpa says?
fw-grandpa-014.back: "A swirl is a no. Back out, come back." Opinion (Tip).

fw-grandpa-017.front: Do deer feed hard before a storm front?
fw-grandpa-017.back: Studies disagree. Penn State found no meaningful effect of oncoming winter storms (75%). Opinion; go when you can.

fw-grandpa-019.back: Temperature (65%, secondary). 'Cold snaps move deer' has some support; a Texas study disagreed.

fw-grandpa-021.back: "... find the animal." Forage best described mule deer feeding sites (85%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-025.back: "... the middle." Where cover meets food (75%). Tradition. On grassland, hunt the folds.

fw-grandpa-026.back: Large forest patches with hiding cover, away from open roads (80%). Go where the pressure is not.

fw-grandpa-027.back: "... scouting report in the valley." 88% of surveyed Idaho landowners say yes when asked first (80%).

fw-grandpa-028.back: "... the light." Bucks often bed early; set up before first light (80%, Mule Deer Foundation).

fw-grandpa-032.front: "If you think you are going slow enough, ..."
fw-grandpa-032.back: "... halve it." 3 to 5 m then stop; or one step every 30 seconds (65 to 75%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-033.back: Head down, you move. Head up, you are a stump. Movement gives you away (85%). Opinion.

fw-grandpa-034.back: Never walk the top. Come up below the crest and peek. A human outline spooks game (85%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-035.back: "... you are a stump." Freeze until it looks away. Opinion (Tip).

fw-grandpa-036.back: "... do the walking." Sit on a trail, pinch or edge. 72% of Penn State hunters sat still in the morning (85%). Opinion.

fw-grandpa-037.back: About 3 days (60%, secondary). The best stand is the one the deer do not know you use.

fw-grandpa-040.front: Still hunting: where do your eyes go at each stop?
fw-grandpa-040.back: Into the woods ahead and to the sides, not at your feet (85%, hunter education). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-041.front: "You can fool the eyes, you can fool the ears, ..."
fw-grandpa-041.back: "... you will never fool the nose." Play the wind. Tradition.

fw-grandpa-042.back: "... then decide." A 4 point buck has 4 tines on one antler, not counting the brow tine (99%, synopsis page 4).

fw-grandpa-043.front: Can you age a buck by points?
fw-grandpa-043.back: No: points are not a reliable age guide (90%, BC account). Read the body before the bone. Opinion.

fw-grandpa-044.back: "... the does. The buck will find them before you find him." Tradition.

fw-grandpa-045.front: A white tail flags and bounds away. Grandpa?
fw-grandpa-045.back: "A flag in the air means goodbye. Let it go." Running shots are poor shots. Tradition.

fw-grandpa-046.front: Spooked mule deer behaviour Grandpa counts on?
fw-grandpa-046.back: It often stops to look back (60%). Old bucks often do not. Tradition.

fw-grandpa-047.front: Daylight buck visits to stand areas, weeks 1 to 3 versus week 13 (one study)?
fw-grandpa-047.back: About 1 in 3, then about 1 in 20 (60%, secondary). Hunt the trail, not the field.

fw-grandpa-063.front: Call to the tail or the face?
fw-grandpa-063.back: The tail. Quiet when birds come at you (70%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-064.front: "If you can see the duck's eye, ..."
fw-grandpa-064.back: "... it can see yours." A bare face or hands flare ducks (70%). Opinion.

fw-grandpa-065.front: When do you stand up on decoying ducks?
fw-grandpa-065.back: When they commit: wings cupped, feet down. Early shots are long shots (65 to 75%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-066.front: Ducks Unlimited: many self taught hunters struggle past what range on crossers?
fw-grandpa-066.back: About 27 m (30 yd) (85%). If you have to wonder if it is in range, it is not.

fw-grandpa-067.front: Covey rise: how many birds do you shoot at?
fw-grandpa-067.back: One, then the next. Pick a single bird (85%, Kentucky wildlife agency). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-068.back: "... before you shoot the next." Mark the fall and go straight to it. Opinion.

fw-grandpa-069.front: Where do you never hunt waterfowl, by tradition?
fw-grandpa-069.back: The roost. Hunting near it can push birds off (65%). Hunt where they feed or fly.

fw-grandpa-070.back: "... not the goose." Set up where they fed the evening before (65%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-071.back: "... miss small." One hair, not the whole deer. Origin unsettled (Tip). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-072.front: "If you can get lower, get lower. If you can get closer, ..."
fw-grandpa-072.back: "... get closer." Close shots forgive errors (75%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-073.back: Yours, not the rifle's. Beyond your competent range you risk crippling (85%, Ducks Unlimited). Opinion.

fw-grandpa-074.back: Broadside or quartering away, still, near leg forward (85%, hunter education). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-075.back: "... then wait it." Use landmarks for where it stood and vanished (85%, National Deer Association).

fw-grandpa-076.front: Liver or gut hit: how long to wait?
fw-grandpa-076.back: Hours, longer than for a lung hit; gut longest. Sources differ: Hunter Ed blog 4 to 6 h and 6 to 8 h; National Deer Association 2012 2 to 4 h and 4 to 6 h; 2023 8 to 10 h and 10 to 12 h (70%). Your call. Pushed early, lost forever.

fw-grandpa-078.front: No blood at the hit site means a miss?
fw-grandpa-078.back: No. Check for hair and bone and search (75%). Read the hit site slowly.

fw-grandpa-079.front: Where do you walk on a blood trail?
fw-grandpa-079.back: Beside it, flagging each spot. You may need it twice (85%). Opinion.

fw-grandpa-080.front: Leg or bone hit: wait or go?
fw-grandpa-080.back: Go now, ready for a follow up shot (85%, National Deer Association). Finish the one you started.

fw-grandpa-082.back: The hide holds heat; removing it lets meat cool faster (90%, Ohio). A hide is a winter coat.

fw-grandpa-083.back: No. Plastic traps heat and moisture; use cloth game bags (65%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-084.front: How long to hang venison at home?
fw-grandpa-084.back: 2 to 3 days at 4 °C or below, at most (90%, Penn State Extension). Aging is not necessary for sausage.

fw-grandpa-085.back: Wet cotton loses insulation and dries slowly (70%). True in cold and wet; overstated on warm days.

fw-grandpa-086.back: "... start cold." Start with fewer layers so you do not sweat; add layers when you stop (70%). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-088.front: Sharp knife or dull knife: which is safer?
fw-grandpa-088.back: Sharp. Dull knives slip and need more force (80%, university extension). Tradition.

fw-grandpa-089.front: Bear country camp: food and meat how far from your bed?
fw-grandpa-089.back: At least 100 m (80%, Alberta BearSmart). A clean camp is a quiet camp.

fw-grandpa-090.front: When do you check your rifle's zero?
fw-grandpa-090.back: Before the season, after a bump, after air travel (65%). Shoot it before you hunt it.
